PubHealthEpi: Health Disparities, Survival Analysis & Causal Inference

An End-to-End Public Health Epidemiology Pipeline

Author

Ludovic Njiosseu, MS Biostatistics

Published

May 19, 2026

Overview

This project builds a complete public health epidemiology pipeline on a simulated longitudinal cohort of 8,000 patients, integrating three analytical modules: claims-based disparity analysis, survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier + Cox PH), and causal inference (IPTW + Doubly Robust AIPW). It replicates methods used in regulatory-grade real-world evidence (RWE) studies and population health research.

Research question: Does receipt of a community health worker intervention reduce time to acute hospitalization, and does this effect persist after adjusting for confounding by insurance status, race/ethnicity, and socioeconomic factors?

Module 1 — Data Construction

Code 
source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
Cohort: 8000 patients | Event rate: 82.9% | Median follow-up: 29.3 months
Intervention rate: 28.1%
Claims: 21157 records across 7808 patients
Saved: data/cohort.csv, data/claims.csv
Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)

The cohort includes patients enrolled 2015–2019 with up to 60 months of follow-up. Key features: demographics, insurance type, poverty area percentage, comorbidity burden (Charlson index), smoking status, BMI, and a binary intervention indicator subject to confounding (intervention uptake is higher among insured and urban patients — a realistic selection mechanism).

ED Utilization by Race/Ethnicity

Code 
ed_race <- read_csv("outputs/ed_by_race.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ed_race %>%
  mutate(race_ethnicity = fct_reorder(race_ethnicity, pct_any_ed)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = race_ethnicity, y = pct_any_ed, fill = race_ethnicity)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(White = "#2980b9", Black = "#e74c3c",
                               Hispanic = "#f39c12", Asian = "#27ae60",
                               Other = "#7f8c8d")) +
  labs(title = "ED Utilization Rate by Race/Ethnicity",
       x = NULL, y = "% with Any ED Visit") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")

Adjusted Predictors of ED Overutilization

Code 
ed_logit <- read_csv("outputs/ed_logistic_regression.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ed_logit %>%
  mutate(variable  = fct_reorder(variable, odds_ratio),
         direction = ifelse(odds_ratio > 1, "Increases Risk", "Decreases Risk"),
         sig       = ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = log(odds_ratio), fill = direction, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increases Risk" = "#e74c3c",
                               "Decreases Risk" = "#2980b9")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = 1, "p ≥ 0.05" = 0.45)) +
  labs(title = "Adjusted Predictors of ED Overutilization",
       x = NULL, y = "Log Odds Ratio", fill = NULL, alpha = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

Being uninsured, Black race/ethnicity, and higher area poverty are associated with significantly elevated ED utilization after adjustment. The intervention is associated with lower ED use.

Kaplan-Meier: Intervention vs Control

Code 
km_int <- read_csv("outputs/km_intervention.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
km_int %>%
  mutate(Group = ifelse(strata == "intervention=0", "Control", "Intervention")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time, y = survival, color = Group, fill = Group)) +
  geom_step(size = 1.1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Control = "#e74c3c", Intervention = "#2980b9")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = c(Control = "#e74c3c", Intervention = "#2980b9")) +
  labs(title = "Time to Hospitalization: Intervention vs Control",
       x = "Months", y = "Hospitalization-Free Survival",
       color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

Cox Proportional Hazards Model

Code 
cox_results <- read_csv("outputs/cox_results.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cox_results %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, hr),
         sig      = ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = hr, ymin = hr_lower95, ymax = hr_upper95,

  geom_pointrange(size = 0.7) +

  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = "#2c3e50", "p ≥ 0.05" = "#7f8c8d")) +
  labs(title = "Cox PH Model: Hazard Ratios (95% CI)",
       x = NULL, y = "Hazard Ratio", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

ps <- read_csv("outputs/propensity_scores.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

  geom_histogram(bins = 40, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +

       x = "Propensity Score", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +

Covariate Balance Before and After IPTW

Code 
balance <- read_csv("outputs/covariate_balance.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
balance %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, abs(smd_unadjusted))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(smd_unadjusted, smd_iptw),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "smd") %>%
  mutate(type = ifelse(type == "smd_unadjusted", "Before IPTW", "After IPTW")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = abs(smd), color = type, group = type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line(alpha = 0.5) + coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Before IPTW" = "#e74c3c", "After IPTW" = "#2980b9")) +
  labs(title = "Covariate Balance: |SMD| Before and After IPTW",
       x = NULL, y = "|Standardized Mean Difference|", color = NULL,
       caption = "Dashed line = 0.10 balance threshold") +
  theme_minimal()

The doubly robust AIPW estimator provides consistent ATE estimates as long as either the propensity score model or the outcome model is correctly specified. The E-value quantifies robustness to unmeasured confounding: an unmeasured confounder would need to be associated with both treatment and outcome by a factor exceeding the E-value to fully explain away the estimated effect.

Reproducibility

install.packages(c("tidyverse", "survival", "shiny", "bslib", "bsicons", "DT"))

source("scripts/01_simulate_data.R")
source("scripts/02_disparity_analysis.R")
source("scripts/03_survival_analysis.R")
source("scripts/04_causal_inference.R")

shiny::runApp("shiny/")
quarto::quarto_render("pubhealth_report.qmd")

Limitations & Extensions

  • Data is simulated; real-world application requires claims linkage, IRB approval, and data use agreements.
  • Cox model assumes proportional hazards; violations for any covariate are flagged via Schoenfeld test and would warrant time-varying coefficient models.
  • IPTW assumes no unmeasured confounding (conditional exchangeability); the E-value provides sensitivity analysis but does not eliminate this limitation.
  • Competing risks (e.g. death before hospitalization) are not modeled; Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models are the appropriate extension.
  • Area-level poverty is used as a proxy for SES; individual-level income, education, and housing data would improve precision.
